exception.reason: Three independently organised directions were tested. Mathematical and computational astrophysics has UCR mathematics, programming, data-science and imaging methods but no astronomy, astrophysics or cumulative physics content; a complete schedule would become a generic mathematics/data programme. Planetary science has Earth-system and remote-sensing analogues but no celestial mechanics, planetary formation, exoplanets, planetary atmospheres or space science. Astronomical observation has transferable image/signal methods but no telescopes, detectors, astronomical spectroscopy or photometry, observing laboratories or astronomy research. Because stars, galaxies, cosmology, planets and their physical explanation are the academic objects rather than a professional qualification, none of these partial method sets sustains a coherent 23-course non-PPD Astronomy response.
exception.curriculumContext: The settled current Astronomy curriculum remains complete at 180 EC. It preserves the required astronomy, physics, mathematics, programming, practical-observing and research sequence; 8 EC of third-year astronomy/research-skills study; the distinct 18+1+3 EC research-project components; and all 30 EC of genuine approved free choice. No first-stage curriculum or language decision is reopened.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including course descriptions or outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and six-semester cohort availability. DISGATE102, DISMATH211, DISMATH213, DISMATH214, DISMATH312 and DISMATH314 provide calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, differential equations, linear systems, probability and statistics. DISGATE101, DISDATA111, DISDATA211, DISDATA212 and DISDATA311 provide programming, data preparation, machine learning, image processing and computer vision. These are real mathematical and computational contributions, but their documented content does not teach astrophysics, stellar structure/evolution, galaxies, cosmology, celestial mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum or statistical physics. ENSENVI111 and ENSENVI213 study the Earth and interactions among its physical spheres; ENSENVI211 applies satellite/drone observation to Earth ecosystems, land cover and climate. They do not teach planets, planetary-system formation, exoplanets or space science. DISDATA212 and DISMATH312 teach cameras, digital filters, features, signals and systems, but not telescopes, astronomical detectors, spectroscopy/photometry, observing practice or reduction of astronomical observations. No workbook row supplies an astronomy/astrophysics sequence or a scheduled astronomy research project. Academic feasibility therefore fails before accepting 24 courses, so no schedule or UCR-credit comparison is fabricated.

candidateAssessment.assessment: UCR supplies substantial calculus, linear algebra, numerical, probability, programming, data and image-analysis methods. It does not supply the stellar, galactic, cosmological or physics sequence that gives those methods an astronomical object, so a complete programme would be generic mathematical data science rather than Astronomy.

Dynamic Earth, Earth System Science Tools and Earth Observation offer genuine Earth-system and remote-sensing analogues. Their documented content remains terrestrial and environmental; it does not establish celestial mechanics, Solar-System science, exoplanets, planetary formation, planetary atmospheres or space science.

Image Processing and Computer Vision and Linear Systems supply transferable imaging and signal methods. They do not teach telescopes, astronomical detectors, spectroscopy or photometry, observing laboratories, astronomical calibration/data reduction or astronomy research, so the direction cannot support a complete observational-astronomy programme.
